Research provenance: Appianing J, Quansah F, Amoako R. DB locales: No live DWS published questionnaire in Supabase app.assessment_versions; no stable/edition key in Master3881 or PR495.

Other translations: Ghana original source/administration context; no independently verified non-English translations or equivalence.
Target population: N1533 university undergraduate and postgraduate students in Ghana; not general adult or clinical norms.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: Article CC BY publication does not by itself establish ownership or rights for hosted commercial digital questionnaire, translations, administration and scored reports. Obtain final 41-item text, authorized scoring, owner commercial online permission and appropriate interpretation before deployment.

Instrument (EN): Climate Change Worry Scale for Adolescents — Canadian adapted five-item edition
Scales / measured domains (EN): Micro-worry (2): self / close others; Macro-worry (3): future generations / people in other countries / animals and nature; two factors
Research provenance: Martin G et al., Journal of Climate Change and Health 2026-08-07 DOI 10.1016/j.joclim.2026.100721. English Canadian adolescent survey N804 ages13–18; CFA complete subset approximately N780, gender/age-group invariance reported; adapted from Ojala five-item Climate Worry Scale. Shares same N804 cohort/DOI with CCIDLS; do NOT treat them as separate validation cohorts.
DB locales: No CWS-A exact study/edition stable key in Master3881, PR495 or live Supabase published key list. This is not the Stewart Climate Change Worry Scale CCWS-10.
EN form: English respondent form studied in Canadian adolescents; this is English adaptation/contextual validation, NOT a validated translation from a non-English language.
Other translations: Canadian study language English only; no independently validated translations or non-Canadian norms.
Target population: Canadian adolescents ages13–18, N804; CFA complete subset about N780; no validation in adult/general clinical samples.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: 2026 article CC BY-NC-ND is noncommercial/non-derivative publication licence; source Ojala item reuse and commercial SaaS digitization/wording/scoring rights separately require written permission, minor consent and privacy safeguards.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY / PERMISSION_REQUIRED. Two-factor affective climate worry, not psychiatric diagnosis or clinical cutoff. Same sample as CCIDLS and no independent retest; minors require consent/safeguarding. Do not reproduce questionnaire or publish.

Instrument (EN): Climate Concern Impact on Daily Life Scale — Canadian adolescent validation
Scales / measured domains (EN): One factor: climate-concern related effects on concentration or schoolwork; sleep; enjoyment of nature; having fun; relationships
Research provenance: Martin G et al., Journal of Climate Change and Health 2026-08-07 DOI 10.1016/j.joclim.2026.100721. Canadian adolescents N804 shared with CWS-A (complete CFA approximately N772); one-factor CFA acceptable CFI with RMSEA near .081, age/gender invariance; cross-sectional item-level IRT; five items retained despite overlap of enjoyment items.
DB locales: Standalone CCIDLS five-item function/impact scale distinct from CWS-A affective two-factor worry measure. Exact key absent Master3881, PR495 and live Supabase published definitions.
EN form: English survey studied with Canadian adolescents; not a newly translated validated English instrument.
Other translations: English original Canadian study; no country-specific non-English respondent validation.
Target population: Same N804 ages13–18 cohort as CWS-A, complete CFA subset about N772; no independent replication or adult norms.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: CC BY-NC-ND article publication not commercial questionnaire licence; clarify instrument rights, final wording, age-appropriate scoring, GDPR/PIPEDA-style minor privacy, parental consent where applicable, and risk-handling before digital use.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY / PERMISSION_REQUIRED. Functioning impacts not a validated diagnosis or medical acuity; no score cutoffs, no automated clinical advice, no publication. Shared N804 not counted twice.

Research provenance: Hoffmann L et al., Physiotherapy Research International 2026, DOI 10.1002/pri.70309; German-speaking physiotherapy, occupational and speech-language therapists.
